set_aside.unit: context: agreement of the earlier states' texts with this state
set_aside.subject: AuditRecord creation for failed significant actions
set_aside.text: “An action is recorded when it completes or, for a snapshot import, when the attempt is classified; an operation that fails on storage or the Registry before that is not recorded (R0-25).” contradicts M36: “every significant action … writes exactly one record,” including grant and assignment management, with `result: success | rejected`.
set_aside.question: When a significant non-import action fails on Registry or persistence before completing, does it create a rejected AuditRecord or no AuditRecord?
options: Create no AuditRecord for any such pre-completion Registry or storage failure
Create one rejected AuditRecord because the attempted action is in the significant-action catalog
Apply the no-record exception only to snapshot import failures covered by R0-25
set_aside.default_guess: Create no AuditRecord, following the newly added explicit blanket sentence, despite M36.

witness.initial: An active administrator and active viewer exist; the viewer has a revoked ProjectViewerGrant for project P, so the one-record-per-pair rule prevents another grant record.
events: The administrator asks the portal to grant viewer access to P again.
The operation passes its Registry check, attempts the second insert, and persistence rejects it because the pair already has a record.
outcomes: No AuditRecord is created because the operation failed on storage before completing.
One rejected `viewer_grant` management AuditRecord is created because M36 says every significant grant-management action writes exactly one record.
witness.observer: An administrator or auditor inspecting the audit history.
